desert_p14_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_001.text: The proposed second journey began with a well account. Bitter Wells sold travelling water from its municipal filling yard, where the rate changed with the queue rather than with the buyer's courage. Han arrived early and found four carriers already arguing over the order. A woman with a blue apron counted the wagons against her chalkboard. She moved Han behind a flour cart because the flour carter had actually been waiting since dawn. Han accepted the place.

desert_p14_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_002.text: Yue stood beside the empty inspected tank and watched the bucket counter lift and fall, each stroke making water briefly visible before it disappeared through the clean covered filling throat. The price had risen since the first hire. A pump bearing needed replacement, and the yard was recovering the repair charge from large travelling sales. Han read the posted notice and asked how long the temporary rate would remain. The woman pointed to the finishing date printed beneath it.

desert_p14_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_003.text: He thanked her, then went back to the cooperative with the revised estimate rather than buy a promise he could not fund. Yue stayed to ask about a reservation for the following week. The woman said she could reserve a filling window against a deposit, not water that had already been drawn. Yue wrote down the distinction and the hour.

desert_p14_004.speaker: han_xun
desert_p14_004.text: I can absorb the cart inspections; they belong to my firm after the collar report. I cannot absorb every other cost and pretend the journey remains properly funded. The well rate adds this amount. A competent stoneworker adds another, and the paper conservator has her own tools to prepare. We can reduce the time spent on objects if we must, but we cannot reduce the drivers' return water to make the figures prettier. If the subscribers want the valley checked, this is what a checked valley costs. I am prepared to be told they no longer want it.

desert_p14_005.speaker: han_xun
desert_p14_005.text: I am less prepared to send Gao out on a flattering lie.

desert_p14_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_006.text: The freight chair listened without interrupting. Beside her sat the rival publisher's representative, who wanted the stoneworker removed because the declared purpose was a route enquiry. Gao asked how he expected them to judge the relay approach if its retaining work had failed. He said measured exterior pictures might suffice. Du asked which picture would tell him whether the narrow passage had support beneath it. The man conceded the specialist, but wanted the interior records work postponed. That proposal at least concerned a real choice.

desert_p14_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_007.text: A conservator could not save pages she was never funded to approach.

desert_p14_008.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_008.text: We can inspect the current channel and the outer route first, then approach the relay only where the stoneworker finds stable access. We need a paper conservator because the report may depend on records that ordinary field hands should not handle. If there are no accessible records, she can examine the exterior storage condition and come home. That is an honest risk in the hire. If the fund cannot carry her, we should say the old records question remains unanswered and keep our scope outside. I would prefer to take her.

desert_p14_009.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_009.text: I will not call an untrained visitor a conservator after the cart leaves.

desert_p14_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_010.text: The chair asked the receiving clerk for the unused expedition contingency from the first account. Some could be released after the keeper's claims check; some remained committed to damaged gear. The sum would not pay for everything. Du offered to fund the conservator's fee from his correction reserve, provided her report remained independent of his map office. The rival representative looked startled and then suspicious. Du showed the reserve entry without revealing the private customers behind it. His offer was partly remorse and partly professional hunger. Yue could see both in the way he kept looking toward the historical letter.

desert_p14_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_011.text: He wanted those pages read, and wanted to be there when they were. The conservator came to the office carrying a narrow wooden box and an umbrella with one repaired spoke. She worked for the town reading house, not for Du. Her first question was whether the old papers could remain in place if removal proved damaging. Gao said that was acceptable within the enquiry. Her second concerned custody if any were already loose and endangered. The district officer's permission would be required, alongside a site inventory and the local keeper's account.

desert_p14_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_012.text: She was not agreeing to private extraction for a publisher. Du said he understood. She watched him until he added that he would pay the same fee if nothing could safely be copied or lifted. The stoneworker was a quiet older mason with a missing front tooth and a habit of leaning on nothing. He studied the north exchange sketch, put his hand over the buried roof, and asked whether anybody had tried to take a loaded cart across it. Gao explained the present restriction. He said the restriction seemed the best part of the drawing.

desert_p14_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_013.text: Then he asked for the current channel grades, knowing they were precisely what the next journey would obtain. His hire included ordinary assessment and small access stabilization within rated equipment; it did not include rebuilding a valley. He would bring a sounding rod, shims and limited cribbing, inspected before departure. Two drivers volunteered from Han's regular list. One had been on the first expedition and knew the ridge; the other drove a municipal stone cart and could handle the longer exposed turns. The farrier would inspect the four mules but remain in town for existing commitments.

desert_p14_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_014.text: Each driver therefore had a checked minor-care kit and instructions for problems beyond it, with paid return time if an animal could not continue. The cook also stayed home. Nine adults could manage a smaller journey's camp meals from prepared dry provisions. Han counted the party aloud: Gao, Tuo if medically cleared, Bao, Du, Yue, two drivers, a stoneworker and a paper conservator. No spare invisible hands would be waiting at camp. Han assigned two larger reserve service tanks, each with a checked usable capacity of six hundred and fifty litres and a separate protected hundred-litre compartment.

desert_p14_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_015.text: Tuo heard the plan from Bao before she heard it from Han. She asked whether there would be a chair on every slope. Bao said there would be a seated travel place and tasks chosen around the examination, or there would be no Tuo. The answer made her bristle. Then she put her foot on the stool without being asked. The swelling had nearly settled, but the outer tenderness remained after longer movement. Bao prescribed another few days of local walking on level ground, followed by a functional review with the town clinician.

desert_p14_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_016.text: Tuo could decide whether she wanted the hire. She could not decide that wanting it made the ankle ready.

desert_p14_017.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p14_017.text: I want to go because I know the valley approach and because my oldest useful road is in danger of becoming one more confident story. I do not want to go to prove I can endure an ankle. If the review says I cannot walk the required ground, Gao should hire another guide and I will draw what I remember here. Tell Han that. He will be grateful to hear it and try to pay me for staying, which I will allow if he actually uses the drawing.

desert_p14_018.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p14_018.text: There is no prize for giving everybody my work free merely because I have become temporarily inconvenient.

desert_p14_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_019.text: The next morning Yue accompanied Tuo on the prescribed level walk to a tea stall. The pace was slow enough to make the stall owner believe they had come to browse. He offered three varieties they did not want and a fourth he hoped they could afford. Tuo sat, ordered the ordinary pot, and began drawing the old narrowing on the back of his discarded wrapping paper. Yue held the corners flat. Her account placed the winter shelter west of the passage, not beside the relay door. She had seen the shelter roof across the valley once through blowing snow.

desert_p14_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_020.text: The mark belonged to that journey and that visibility, which she wrote beneath it. A little boy at the next bench watched Yue's practice lead protruding from her habitual pack and asked whether it was a snake. She said it was a lead for a receiving apparatus. He asked whether a snake would improve it. Tuo nearly spilled her tea. Yue let him look at the outside without letting him handle it; the stall owner collected him before the boy could recruit another snake. The interruption left Tuo smiling.

desert_p14_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_021.text: She said cultivators ought to employ more children to name their equipment. Yue said they would soon be practising the Great Bowl of Noodles. Tuo replied that many respectable men already did, with less interruption discipline than they claimed. Yue spent the afternoon at a local cultivation room whose custodian rented a guarded receiving station by the session. She showed her kiln certificate and was offered a checked apparatus compatible with her practice lead. The custodian did not propose a new rank.

desert_p14_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_022.text: After ordinary food, sleep and recovery checks, Yue made one brief familiar paired-route task within her established input ceiling, interrupted it cleanly, and rested. The station registered the bounded result. What satisfied her was not the number alone, but the absence of the road's imagined urgency in her hands. She paid for the session, cleaned the outside lead, and left before fatigue could make another trial seem necessary. Outside the practice room, a young apprentice asked how long she had spent earning the fifth stage. Yue said longer than she wanted and no longer than the work required.

desert_p14_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_023.text: He found this evasive. She gave him the months at the kiln, the recovered trials and the next-day checks, and he found that answer discouraging. Then he asked whether it had made her good at caravan work. She said the best thing she had done during the recent break was hold a cover where the farrier needed it. The apprentice frowned, imagining a farrier in the middle of a cultivation examination. Yue bought him a sesame cake before the frown became permanent. Han's mother kept her clinic appointment on the day his carts went through inspection.

desert_p14_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_024.text: He took her himself, carrying her shawl despite her insistence that she still possessed arms. In the waiting room she told him that she disliked having her cough discussed by every neighbour, and liked the neighbour who brought broth without discussing it. He noted the distinction. The clinician adjusted the household care schedule and asked for a later review. Nothing in the visit promised a sudden cure. When they came home, his mother chose the seat by the basil and told him to open the bills.

desert_p14_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_025.text: She preferred to watch him complain about arithmetic to hear him deny that he was worried. The accounts exposed a late payment from a grain client. Han had been treating it as imminent for two weeks. His daughter found the client's last letter and pointed to the sentence saying after resale. He had read it as after arrival. The error was small enough to resemble optimism and large enough to make the new hire uncomfortable. He wrote to the client requesting a dated partial settlement, then reduced the amount he offered from his own reserve.

desert_p14_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_026.text: The cooperative could either fill the gap or shrink the scope. His daughter watched him place the revised sum in the proposal and looked unexpectedly proud. He was learning to come home before he left.

desert_p14_027.speaker: han_xun
desert_p14_027.text: I have corrected my contribution. This is the amount the firm can release now, not the amount it may collect from a customer later. I will guarantee the return provision from the separate account already held at the receiving house. The new work still needs the remainder shown here. You may use a different factor if mine is too little. But if you use mine, I want it written once and paid once. My daughter has become intolerable about letters, and she is right.

desert_p14_028.speaker: han_xun
desert_p14_028.text: I would rather suffer her at the kitchen table than discover the same error halfway to Onion Hollow.

desert_p14_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_029.text: The cooperative filled part of the gap from a route-maintenance fund approved by its members. The rival publisher paid the other part after the chair gave him a signed equal-release clause. No contribution acquired a deed over the valley well. The district office issued a limited exterior route and channel enquiry, with conditional access to the relay site under the mason's assessment and the records officer's custody terms. The valley's actual residents could identify occupied ground and private stores when the party arrived. Gao read the scope aloud to the nine proposed travellers.

desert_p14_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_030.text: Yue found it less exhilarating than the town's palace tale and much more capable of getting them home. The cropped field inspection took place while the new commission was still being signed. The deputy walked the drain with the woman representative and her brother, recorded the present marks, and compared them with the quarry's berm account. He found a plausible diverted contribution but reserved the final assessment for levels at the junction. The woman came back to town with muddy boots and a dated inspection slip.

desert_p14_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_031.text: She brought Han a mat corner repaired so cleverly that the old bend barely showed. It was a sale sample, she explained, not a gift. He ordered two for his receiving bench and paid the stated rate. Neither had to pretend this settled the crop. Gao wanted a replacement instrument rod before departure. Her old threaded coupling had acquired a slight play, not enough to explain every field difference but enough to warrant retirement from the long baseline work. The instrument maker offered a finer imported rod at a price that would consume the team's repair contingency.

desert_p14_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_032.text: She selected the plain local replacement, checked its length against the shop reference and had its coupling marked. Yue expected her to regret the finer one. Gao did, openly, all the way to the door. She could like excellent tools without sending the party into the valley with no money left for a broken ordinary wheel. The conservator's box held thin support boards, clean sleeves, small weights, soft brushes and a limited humidity shelter for temporary handling. She showed Yue how a support went beneath a loose page and how easily an eager fingertip could break a dry edge.

desert_p14_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_033.text: Yue practised on modern discarded paper at the reading house until she stopped trying to help by pulling. The conservator said she could assist with carrying and labelled custody, but the old materials would remain under professional handling. Du watched from the doorway, fingers tucked behind his back. His restraint looked physical, almost comic. Yue imagined his hands tied there with invisible thread and had to look away before she smiled. The mason inspected the proposed cribbing and selected fewer pieces than Han offered.

desert_p14_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_034.text: Weight was not the only question; a short sound block was worth more than a long soft one. He rejected two boards with hidden rot and asked the driver to place the accepted pieces low over the axle. The conservator's dry box rode higher, away from the tank fittings, within its own strapped carrier. Gao's tripod and replacement rod had separate padded slots. The inspected carts held their loads with room for the travellers' ordinary seated places. Their passenger limits were recorded; rescue transport, if required, would displace equipment and change the load plan rather than conjure a fourth seat.

desert_p14_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_035.text: Bao purchased fresh field screening sets and a sealed medical refill from the clinic supplier. She checked the stated batch dates, controls and remaining capacities rather than accepting the supplier's cheerful claim that the desert cured everything by drying it out. Her treatment water allowance belonged within the team's travelling stock. Extra need would change actual withdrawals. The kit also held dressings for ordinary hands, an ankle support and a compact splint suitable for initial stabilization, not a complete clinic. Yue carried the dry package to the yard and put it where Bao directed.

desert_p14_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_036.text: The supplier called after them that he had meant the drying remark as a joke. Bao said he should improve his jokes. They bought nine days of dry food for a planned six-day circuit, including contingency, and forty kilograms of cooking fuel in measured bags. There was no promise that an inhabited valley would feed them. The water forecast covered nine adults and four mules: one hundred and seventeen litres in an ordinary day, with a six-day plan leaving margin for heat, treatment and delay. The initial stock would be thirteen hundred usable litres, including two protected hundred-litre compartments.

desert_p14_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_037.text: Gao had no intention of spending all the margin merely because it existed. Yue watched the smaller party's packing and felt how each absent worker became a task someone else would need to do. The first driver's wife sent prepared flatbread for the departure breakfast, wrapped in a cloth bearing their household mark. It was a gift to be eaten, with the cloth to return. The driver wrote his own family's planned message day beside Han's dispatch schedule. He had learned on the first journey how quickly a late caravan became a frightening story at home.

desert_p14_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_038.text: The second driver asked for a duplicate note to his municipal employer. Gao agreed to send the common arrival report through the first real courier they found. She did not promise an invented daily messenger. Both drivers preferred an honest interval to an impressive silence broken only when somebody was hurt. Bao and the town clinician reviewed Tuo after several days of level walking and rest. The guide could bear weight and turn on firm ground without sharp pain; her remaining limit was prolonged rough walking or carrying.

desert_p14_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_039.text: The clinical plan allowed a seated route role, short observed approach work and renewed checks if symptoms returned. It did not send her into the relay's broken interior. Tuo read the written limits, argued about one adjective, and accepted the rest. The mason said he would assess the access with Gao while she guided from firm positions. She replied that he was welcome to every bad floor in the valley. The hire could proceed.

desert_p14_040.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p14_040.text: Onion Hollow has a spring festival if the households are still there. They hang onion skins from the willows and tell strangers the trees bloom twice. I believed them the first time, which Du has never allowed me to forget. The outer track rises before the narrowing; a low cart can turn at the shoulder if the old rock remains. We will inspect it now rather than argue with my childhood. I want us to arrive as people asking after a place. Do not let the town send us in as treasure hunters.

desert_p14_041.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p14_041.text: There are few faster ways to make an ordinary family hide its door from you.

desert_p14_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_042.text: On the filling morning, the municipal keeper checked both clean tank throats and began the measured transfer at the reserved hour. The tested yard supply entered two six-hundred-and-fifty-litre loads, usable capacity confirmed after filling. Each tank held a hundred litres in its protected compartment, included in the total. Han witnessed the count with Gao and the drivers. The two loaned quarry casks remained returned; they were neither in the carts nor secretly waiting to enlarge the capacity. Bao sealed the common supply record after the source keeper signed it.

desert_p14_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_043.text: Yue had watched too much water become an assumption on the first trip to find the ordinary filling dull. The departure table held nine signed hire slips, the route scope, return funds and a little flower drawing Han had decided to keep at home. He checked the last gear receipts with Yue. Her salt hat, measuring flags and issued cloak were lent again under the new term, while her ordinary sword, notebook and practice lead were still her own. No equipment became hers merely because she had washed it. She packed the repaired cloak with pleasure anyway.

desert_p14_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_044.text: Outside, the drivers settled the four mules into their two pairs. The town had enough stories now. The party was ready to go and obtain a place those stories could answer to. Han walked with them only as far as the Black Gate. His mother watched from the household window; his daughter stood beside him carrying a basket that was finally empty of drawings. At the gate, he gave Gao the receiving-house contact and shook each driver's hand. He did not climb into a cart. Yue looked back once as the road widened.

desert_p14_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_045.text: He was still there, a man in a brown coat beside the newly repaired jamb, smaller already than the scale he had occupied at the head of the first caravan. Then his daughter took his arm and turned him toward town. Their second journey began with that ordinary, difficult act of staying. This departure came seventeen days after their first morning on the road. The intervening week had not repaired every dispute, but it had repaired one approach. At the route office's notice board, Gao checked the temporary deck over the flood-damaged causeway.

desert_p14_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_046.text: Its stone abutments had remained sound; a rated timber span now crossed the failed surface while longer work waited. The inspection notice named the cart limits and the opening date. Both loaded vehicles fell within those limits. The public approach would shorten the journey to the grass village. Tuo inspected the turn when they reached it anyway, pleased to find a change she had not needed to remember. The deck smelled of fresh cut timber in the morning heat.

desert_p14_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_047.text: A route worker waved them into the waiting space and let an empty local wagon clear the far end before their first cart approached. The driver took his pair across at the posted pace, with no second cart on the span beside him. Yue walked by the firm marked edge only where the worker allowed it. Beneath the boards, muddy water carried a twig downstream at surprising speed. The twig struck a stone, turned once and vanished. Yue looked up at the crossing cart, its tank straps neat, its driver watching the line ahead.

desert_p14_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_048.text: New work had earned its ordinary weight. A child on the far bank tried to sell them whistles made from willow. The first driver asked whether they would frighten his mules. The child said only bad mules. This failed to recommend the whistles. The conservator bought one anyway and put it in her outside pocket, perhaps for somebody at home. The mason said the deck's cross-bracing looked well placed, then told the route worker where a rope end was rubbing against a board edge. The worker moved it and thanked him.

desert_p14_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_049.text: It was the kind of exchange Yue liked most on roads: a useful eye, a small repair, nobody required to become the owner of the whole crossing. Beyond the causeway, the village's fields lay brighter than the gravel. Some rows had been replanted. Others remained bare with their disputed marks still visible. Gao stopped at the receiving shed, where a clerk had brought the deputy's initial level report for the collective to examine. The paper supported a contribution from the diversion but did not assign every patch of loss to one cause.

desert_p14_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_050.text: The village woman was angry at its cautious wording and relieved by its attached figures. She asked Gao whether she could use the report in the claim. Gao said the receiving office could tell her the filing form; she could explain the measurements if needed. They sat down together beneath a reed screen. The woman had expected the figures to be either a victory or a rejection. Gao turned the report and showed her the comparison points. The marked low row had received flow after the berm opened; the upper dry row had suffered another problem. The woman recognised both.

desert_p14_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_051.text: Her brother had never claimed the upper row was flooded, although a neighbour had begun saying so for him. She looked embarrassed and then angry at the neighbour. Gao suggested keeping the brother's own field account beside the report. The woman fetched it immediately. The room acquired a clearer claim without anybody becoming less entitled to be upset.

desert_p14_052.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p14_052.text: We will go east after the quarry, toward the narrowing and Onion Hollow. I remember the outer track from years ago. You may have heard more recently from someone who actually travelled it. If you have, tell Gao which day and what load they carried. She will mark it as a current account, not make my old sketch win by seniority. I am also interested in who is living beside the well. A name on a municipal trace is a poor companion when you arrive needing to ask whether a gate is somebody's yard.

desert_p14_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_053.text: The mat maker knew a woman who traded onion cord from the valley. She had passed through the market ten days earlier with two neighbours. Her wagon was light, its animals accustomed to the route; she had reported a damp patch beside the outer cut, not a collapsed road. He described the place she meant using a distinctive split boulder. Gao compared the description with Du's letter and left the relation provisional until they saw the boulder. The mat maker could name the traveller and her market day, which gave the account somewhere to be checked.

desert_p14_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_054.text: Tuo asked whether the woman still made the onion-skin festival flowers. He said she sold them as far as town. They lunched in the shade of the collective's screen rack. The nine travellers ate their own provisions, sharing a little pickle the mat maker sold them from his household jar. The cook's absence became real when no one could agree who had packed the spoon. Yue found it beneath the bread cloth, where the first driver's wife had placed it sensibly. The conservator proposed that they praise the wife before accusing the cloth.

desert_p14_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_055.text: Du tried to praise both and got pickle on his cuff. For once Gao did not reach for a field note. She handed him a scrap of washing rag and let lunch remain lunch. The village carter brought an empty handcart to show the mason the bent wheel that made the ridge expensive. He wanted a repair estimate, not a ruin inspection, and was disappointed to learn that the mason was not a wheelwright. The second driver examined the spoke seat and directed him to Han's town workshop, where the carpenter could assess it properly.

desert_p14_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_056.text: The carter asked whether mentioning the expedition would lower the price. The driver said it might improve the conversation and would not change the wood. The answer amused the carter enough that he offered a fresh route observation in return: the upper bend beyond the village had settled after the recent rain. They inspected that bend before crossing. Settlement had formed a shallow lip, easily visible from the approach now the dust was dry. The leading driver chose the firm outer line under Gao's observation.

desert_p14_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_057.text: Tuo stayed seated where the load plan allowed, refusing the urge to hop down every time a turn interested her. Bao watched the foot's colour and asked about discomfort at the next stop. There was none beyond familiar stiffness. Yue collected the survey flags after Gao completed the short level check, careful not to leave a marker that a local carrier might mistake for a permanent route instruction. The mat maker waved them out from the ridge behind. The country east of the village looked greener from a cart than it felt underfoot.

desert_p14_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_058.text: Low fleabane grew in dusty fans between stones, each patch separated by more bare ground than its distant colour admitted. Lizards flashed through the roots. One stood so still on a hot slab that Du took it for a broken carving until its throat moved. The conservator asked him whether it needed a custody slip. He said only if the lizard intended to publish his observation. Yue laughed, startling the animal into flight. It vanished into a crack no paper would fit. The desert remained perfectly willing to keep some of its inhabitants beyond their enquiry.

desert_p14_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_059.text: Gao worked with the replacement rod at a scheduled halt, checking an ordinary baseline and the coupling's seated mark. The mason held the far end while Yue moved the flags. He spoke very little, which made Gao speak more; she filled the silence with explanations of her instrument until he pointed out that the mark had already agreed twice. She stopped, smiled at herself and put the rod away. Du had watched the exchange with interest. He told her that her uncle had done the same thing when nervous about a new tool. She asked how he knew her uncle.

desert_p14_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_060.text: He said he had bought maps. Everybody's relatives seemed to have bought maps from him eventually.

desert_p14_061.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_061.text: My uncle bought maps because he was too proud to ask directions in a village where he had married somebody's niece. He would prefer that story kept out of your next edition. And yes, I talk too much about a new coupling when I want it to be good. The old one deserved retirement, and the plain replacement deserves an honest trial. You may remind me of that after it passes. Before it passes, I reserve the right to make the stoneworker tired of every word I know about metal. He has been remarkably kind so far.

desert_p14_062.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_062.text: Perhaps he has forgotten where I keep the second rod.

desert_p14_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_063.text: The second driver had taken the municipal employer's leave reluctantly. He was paid reliably there and liked going home before sunset. This commission offered a larger fee and an exposed road whose interest he did not entirely trust. At the afternoon halt, Yue asked why he had accepted. His youngest brother wanted a trade course at the town school. The driver had already agreed to contribute, and the course deposit fell due next month. He said it without turning his brother into a burden. Then he asked Yue whether cultivation schooling cost as much as people claimed.

desert_p14_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_064.text: She answered with the fees she remembered and the months that could not be bought. The driver listened more closely to the months than the coins. His brother wanted to earn quickly, which was not the same thing as refusing work. Yue described the kiln's long waiting between recovered trials, the ordinary jobs that kept a body useful, and the teachers who had stopped her when she wanted progress to resemble hurry. He said the school had told his brother something similar about metalwork. Their conversation ended when a mule pressed its head against his shoulder.

desert_p14_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_065.text: He stroked the animal's cheek and checked the harness line. There was no need to make the agreement larger than two people discovering that somebody else also had to wait. Late light brought a broad stony shoulder into view, sheltered from the north wind by a low rock fin. The drivers preferred it to the old broken quarry shelter because there was room to turn both carts on firm ground. Gao examined the drainage line before approving camp. The mason tapped a loose slab near the proposed stove and shifted the stove site away from it.

desert_p14_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_066.text: Bao chose a clean treatment corner uphill of the animal tether line. Tuo directed the approaching path from her seated place, then took a short permitted walk beside the rock. Her stride was nearly even. Bao called her back before nearly became a reason to wander. Making supper as a smaller crew proved unexpectedly social. The conservator had packed a spice pinch in a paper twist and offered it to the lentils. Du believed he could improve the stove draft with a stone that did not fit the opening. Yue removed the stone before the smoke found Bao.

desert_p14_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_067.text: The mason, who had watched without comment, selected a smaller piece and seated it correctly. Du thanked him with a dignity the others politely ignored. Gao counted out the food portions. Their first shared meal tasted of cumin and slightly scorched ambition. There was enough for everyone, and the second driver asked for the recipe as if the scorching were intentional. The western sky held a long violet streak after sunset. Beneath it the grass village's small lights appeared and vanished when people moved behind their screens.

desert_p14_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_068.text: Yue had seen the same lights on the first journey as signs of a detour. Now she knew the mat maker's table and the woman who carried her brother's claim. The distance between those two ways of seeing a place seemed larger than the road itself. She opened her notebook and drew the rock fin above camp, not particularly well. The conservator looked over her shoulder and asked whether the fin was another lizard. Yue said it had better remain still, because she could not redraw it in flight.

desert_p14_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_069.text: Du took his old letter out after the meal, using a modern copy for the common discussion while the original stayed in its sleeve. The second gate was called a spill throat in one line and a freight constriction in another. Tuo had thought of it as the place where winter wind cut through a cart cover. The mason wanted to know whether the two meanings referred to a shared structure or neighboring works. Gao marked that question for the actual approach. The words had spent years behaving as if everyone knew their surroundings.

desert_p14_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_070.text: Around this new camp they finally had to explain themselves to people who did not.

desert_p14_071.speaker: du_she
desert_p14_071.text: When the relay office closed, its records were supposed to be transferred south. Some inventories did reach the municipal house; other packets remained in the north exchange case. The letter says a storm delayed the valley transfer. It does not say where every packet ended. I had treated that as a dead file because the route no longer brought paying readers. Now the channel may be active again and the residents may still be there. The same old inventory could matter differently.

desert_p14_072.speaker: du_she
desert_p14_072.text: I would like to find the missing sequence, but I will have to live with whatever the conservator says is actually accessible.

desert_p14_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_073.text: The conservator asked why the missing papers mattered to him. He answered too quickly that they might explain the route history. She waited. After a while he said he had helped prepare the clean edition that made the old office seem finished. Finding what had not finished would give him a chance to correct more than a symbol. She nodded without promising the papers would reward him. The mason asked whether the channel's live path might matter more than an inventory. Du said yes. It sounded easy to say beside a pot of lentils.

desert_p14_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_074.text: Yue wondered how easy it would sound at a door full of old pages. Tuo had brought a square of plain cloth as well as her brother's bordered piece. She used the plain square to wrap her ankle support in the evening, reserving the other for herself rather than hanging it as a camp ornament. Bao asked whether she had slept better at home. Tuo said she had slept noisier: a neighbour's nephew had continued fixing the chair after it was fixed. Here the wind occupied a simpler space.

desert_p14_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_075.text: She rubbed the joint where the vine's shadow had fallen at home and asked Bao to let her know if she began treating the foot as an enemy again. Bao said she had already noticed that habit and would. Bao's reason for accepting the second hire came out when the drivers asked about the medical kit. She wanted a small seasonal practice beyond the town clinic, where field workers often waited too long to ask for help. She needed experience with route conditions and a realistic account of supply costs before she could propose it.

desert_p14_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_076.text: This journey paid her properly to learn some of that. The first driver said his wife would welcome a clinic closer to the road work. Bao asked which work sites and which months. He named them. She wrote the names on a private planning page, distinct from the patients' records and the expedition's public report.

desert_p14_077.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p14_077.text: If I open a seasonal room, it must have dependable water, clean storage and a way to transfer a patient who needs more than I can provide. A kind signboard will not do those things. People keep offering me unused sheds as if any roof were a clinic. Some might work after repairs; some cannot. I want to see the village approaches and speak to the actual households before I put my name above one. The second journey helps with that. You can tell your wife I am interested.

desert_p14_078.speaker: bao_sun
desert_p14_078.text: Please also tell her I have not opened anything yet, or I will come home to a queue beside somebody's hens.

desert_p14_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_079.text: Gao asked the conservator what she hoped to find. The woman said a room where the roof had not been treated as an honorary lid. She had spent the spring saving a marriage register from a leaking store, only to have its owner move it back beneath the same cracked tile. Du laughed, then recognized himself in the care for pages without their building. The mason made a rare joke: he offered to charge separately for honorary roofs. It took Yue a second to see that he was smiling. The common fire drew each traveller out a little.

desert_p14_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_080.text: They were becoming nine people rather than a budget of nine adults. Before dark fully settled, the drivers checked the mules' feet and watered them from the measured daily draws. The municipal driver's pair took longer because one animal disliked the unfamiliar tether. He moved the rope to a calmer angle and stood nearby while it drank. Yue held the empty bucket at his direction. She liked the heavy sound of an animal swallowing after a road day, a sound with no mystery in it and plenty of need. The protected compartments remained sealed.

desert_p14_081.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_081.text: Their red threads looked like two tiny pieces of town carried into the night. Everything ordinary had travelled farther than it seemed. The water book closed at eleven hundred and eighty litres after one hundred and twenty drawn that day. The extra three above the ordinary forecast came from actual heat and washing needs, not an attempt to force every day into the same allowance. Each cart held five hundred and ninety litres, including its protected hundred. Bao and Gao checked the figures with the drivers.

desert_p14_082.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_082.text: Four kilograms of fuel used for supper and the next morning's preparation left thirty-six of the purchased forty. There had been no new source draw, no rain catch credited and no spare cask invented. Yue put the count away before it could become the only thing she remembered of their first evening. The willow whistle sounded once after the lantern was lowered. The conservator had meant to test it privately and was embarrassed by how far the note carried. A mule raised its head; the first driver made a stern face that dissolved before he could sustain it.

desert_p14_083.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_083.text: She said she had bought the whistle for her sister's child, whose collection already annoyed three neighbours. Tuo said the child deserved a new target. The conservator wrapped it again, smiling. Beyond camp, an owl called from the ridge in a tone that suggested no appreciation for human instruments. Du asked whether they ought to add it to the field inventory. This time the mason answered him with an actual laugh. Yue took the first watch beside Gao. The task was ordinary camp observation and a check that the stove had cooled safely, not a vigil against imagined desert monsters.

desert_p14_084.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_084.text: Clouds had dissolved into a wide star field. Gao pointed out a constellation her father had called the Broken Ladder; Yue knew it by another name from a different village. They did not settle which was correct. Gao said her father had repaired ladders badly, so perhaps his name contained local evidence. Yue laughed softly enough not to wake the drivers. The dark around them held stone, grass and the road ahead, without requiring a single secret underneath every sound.

desert_p14_085.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_085.text: I used to think the best survey would remove every disagreement. We would measure once, draw cleanly and people would stop arguing because the answer was there. Now I think I might prefer a survey that leaves the right argument in the right place. The collective can argue about a freight ground without wondering which roof we meant. Du can argue with a printer without losing the actual letter. I can argue with my licensing office without pretending the old coupling never worried me. That still sounds tiresome, I know.

desert_p14_086.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p14_086.text: But tonight it sounds possible, which is an improvement on several afternoons I have had recently.

desert_p14_087.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_087.text: The second driver relieved them at the agreed hour. He had slept lightly, still accustomed to his municipal dawn schedule, and brought his blanket around his shoulders like a small tent. Gao handed him the quiet camp account. Yue checked that Tuo's foot remained supported before she lay down; the guide opened one eye and told her to stop practising Bao's face. Yue obeyed. The ground beneath the bedroll was firm, the cloak warm enough in the cooling air. She could smell the cumin twist near the packed food.

desert_p14_088.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_088.text: The new expedition's first night had fewer people and more room for their voices. Tomorrow they would go beyond the road the first one had learned. At the edge of sleep she heard Du turn inside his blanket and the conservator ask him whether the old letter was safely sleeved. He answered yes. A pause followed, then he asked whether she would let him carry the support boards when they reached the relay. She said he could carry them as well as anybody after instruction. He thanked her, sounding younger than his sixty years. Yue closed her eyes.

desert_p14_089.speaker: narrator
desert_p14_089.text: Under the shelf of stars, the party's wants remained distinct: a safe route, an independent finding, a living practice, a brother's school fee, old pages that might still speak. They were going to the same valley for different reasons. That would matter there.
